ABSENCE: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_canonical_outbound_equivalence.py only covers status='closed' (a round-trippable value); no blocked/cancelled/deleted equivalence case
dropped.finding: Status is a LOSSY local→Jira mapping (blocked→'In Progress', cancelled/deleted→'Done'), but the new canonical path compares in LOCAL status space (ticket.status vs canonical_remote['status']), so a locally-'blocked' ticket whose remote reflects 'In Progress' now diffs ('blocked' != 'in_progress') and re-emits a status mutation every pass. The pre-625b differ compared Jira-name to Jira-name ('In Progress' == 'In Progress') and converged with no emit. Convergence in the new path depends on the rebar-status:blocked annotation label being present in the snapshot to override the canonical status — a dependency the old field-diff did not have.
scenarios: A ticket set to status 'blocked' (or 'cancelled') locally, once its Jira counterpart is 'In Progress'/'Done', re-emits an outbound status update on every reconcile pass unless the rebar-status: label happens to be in the snapshot.
dropped.suggested_fix: Compare status by round-tripping local status through the outbound mapper to remote shape and back (or compare the local→Jira mapped name against the raw remote status name) so many-to-one statuses converge as they did pre-625b; alternatively fold the rebar-status label into canonical status before diffing so both sides agree.
